Large, almost clot-shaped pearl of glass flux. The decor is divided into square fields with red streaks in between. Every second field is chessy in yellow and black and every two is blue with a white flower.
Iron ore, 10 dct. Long round gauge neck, slightly upturned. The ring is missing. On the outside of the buttocks and neck, minuskel-m was punched out.

Key fragments of bronze, probably from younger Iron Age. Flag-shaped ax with two spikes on each side. The handle starts with ribbon patterns running around the shaft to then transition to hollow-patterned ornamented fabric.
Oval buckle of Cu alloy, consisting of two consecutive “shells.” The upper has broken decor with animal ornamentation and five buds, as well as two coarse layers of iron.

Oval buckle of gilded Cu alloy. Decor with braids and animal ornamentation and originally nine strapped buds (two missing). Underside with traces of the needle’s attachment and hook, as well as a storage associated with preservation (?).

Reflective buckle of Cu alloy. Ornamented in the form of the three norns (or three bears?) with the heads facing the central part of the span. On the back are remnants of the bracket and iron needle, as well as part of a suspension loop.
Round costume fibula of Cu alloy. Decor of winding, linear bands. Central is a square with a slight elevation. The outer edge smooth, but slightly succumbs to four opposite sides.
The bowl pit stone of eliptically shaped rock, with an oval, soft-shaped recess at the top.
Lancet-shaped, flathuggen, grey flint doc. The tip passes into a shaft with Romani cross section. Type II of Lomborg’s six types of fint daggers (after Lomborg 1973).

Tutulus av brons. Toppen avbruten och stora delar av kanten bortbruten. Täta koncentriska cirklar upp mot toppen. Avbrutet fäste i form av en bronstorne på undersidan. Troligen bronsålderns persod II-III.
Double beer with oval frames, which are slightly convex curved. One frame has a hint of a blunt tip.
Bronze crane patch including beer male in position The Ölhanen shaped like a rooster (the star, however, incomplete) The wooden holder is multi-edged and provided with a protrusion.
Plate tray, possibly used as a pollen or game tray. Something irregular round. A smooth surface but with a brownish coating. On one side with textile prints.
Flat ring, slightly irregular and with traces after filming. Cast. The towers are missing.
Fragment of a ring bell consisting of an edge piece with an outside hull edge. The inside is very nutty.
Handle for a boiler. Wide Rounded Base Party with Three Nights. Flat. The outer end widened.

Knife shaft with residue of an iron toe. On each side of the shaft, two pieces are richly ornate, but strongly corrogated, fastened bronze blacks. One of the signs of interruption and both are distorted.
Round, flat, on the upper side striated ring that has had a smaller loop at one side.
Rund, platt och strierad eller möjligen vriden bronsring som har haft en mindre ögla eller ett utskott vid ena sidan. Vittrande.

Ornerat knivskaft med tånge av järn. Träbeklädnad samt en beklädnad av bronsband med gjutna ornamnet på två sidor. Dessa hålls fast av tre bronsnitar. De gjutna ornamenten visar blomkandelabrar på tvärstreckad botten.

Ornate knife shank with iron toe. Wooden cladding and a cladding of bronze ribbons with cast snake names on two sides. These are held by bronze cutters. A gray-white, calcareous coating conceals parts of the ornaments.
Ornamental seizure of bronze badges, with inter alia a fantasy coat of arms with three leaves.
Ornamental trimmings, or a part of a beech ribbon clasp, consisting of a double weight bleckremsa attached to a rivet at the base. The front of the fittings is adorned with parallel lace angles.
Fragment av kanon. Del av ett profilerat ändparti. På insidan finns en rest av en rätvinklig urtagning. Ändknopp?
Shelf with ordinary shape. Of round thread. Funnen on the stallhold, North side.
Ändparti av ett svagt koniskt bronsrör. Möjligen den distala delen av en krantapp till en ölhane.
Ett förböjt fragment av dubbel kopparplåt med en fastsittande nit. Möjligen takplåt.
Nit av koppar med runt, hamrat, något konvext huvud. Själva niten är konisk och avbruten i spetsen.

A complete bronze suit chain with a 5.8 cm long tree needle at one end. The tree needle has engraved edge lines on the flat part and the end is engraved with lines as well as fields of zigzag patterns.

A band-shaped beech ribbon clasp with a hook. Widowed base with a fitting and two rivets for the mount. Similar to M 17000-1938 with simple, but with slightly more distinctive, ornamentation and profiling.
Rektangulär nitbricka av koppar med avskurna eller avnötta hörn. Runt hål. Förböjd.
Stödknapp i form av ett kvadratiskt bleck med driven (nu tillplattad) mittbuckla, samt ett nithål i vardera hörn.
Ändparti av ett svagt koniskt bronsrör. Möjligen den distala delen av en krantapp till en ölhane.
Kvadratiskt prydnadsbelsag av brons, möjligen till ett bokband. Genombrutet mönster med fyra hörnställda liljor omkring ett runt mitthål.

Solid, slightly conical cylinder of bronze with two committees. Around the middle hole and through this one at the narrower end fixed shaft of iron. The shaft interrupted and heavily rust-damaged. Possibly a lock or a warehouse?

Fragment of a candlestick in the shape of a profiled edge piece. Possibly from a round drop bowl or foot, adorned with engraved parallel lines. Very smooth and smooth surface, even inside. May also be an edge to a bronze vessel.
Fragment of a cannon. Partly melted break piece of end knob or similar. Rounded and with an ornamental vulst. On the underside traces after a probably five-sided recess.
Troligen rund kopparten, men ursprunglig form omöjlig att bestämma på grund av oxidering och föroreningar (sand etc).

Triangulärt prydnadsbleck av silver som dock är avbrutet längs ena sidan. Från mitten och nedåt är små drivna bucklor, varav den största har en mittknopp. Utifrån bucklorna går graverade raka och vågiga linjer.
Fragments of some oval medallion of blank polished jet, or pitch carbon and gagate as it is also called. The badge is now in two parts and about 1/4 of the medallion is completely missing.
Spetsigt remändbeslag av tenn med rund ändknopp. Ihålig och gjuten i två halvor. Nitrester av järn. Framsidan har bladornament på finrutad botten, baksidan grövre rutmönster, delvis bortbrutet.
Fragment av oregelbundet rund blyplåt med ett utskott vid ena sidan. Några stämpelavtryck ej urskiljbara. Sannolikt ena halvan av en blyplomb.
Yttre delen av ovalt benskaft med kvarsittande del av tånge. Vid änden tre parallella graverade linjer. Tillverkad av ett rörben.
Sölja av bronsbleck med torne och fyrsidig ram. Ytterkanten ornerad med två par inskärningar samt en rad av fem instämplade runda gropar. Även tornen av bleck.
Conical roof spike of copper. Hollow and with lace oval head. Strong white spirit.
Cylindriskt blylod eller sänke med ögla av mässingstråd. Blyplattan är rullad och hamrad. Vasatid/tidigmodern tid? Snöret sekundärt.
Oregelbundet klippt plåt med en rak kant. Hoprullad och hopklämd. Vid kanten en grupp spikhål.
The top of the burner boiler. It is made from round, down a slightly tapered boiler of hammered copper sheet. Composed of rivets and with wall cylinder that encloses the upper part of the object.
The years 1935 - 1943 extensive conservation and restoration work was carried out on Kronoberg Castle Ruin (Swedish Heritage Board 93 in Växjö sn) and in connection with it archaeological studies.
Part of a wheeled, breakthrough ornamental fitting, altenatively an amulet in lead. A centrally located around holes and four of originally six remaining “spokes.” A third of the object is broken.
Nose next to the granite cannonball. The surface is seemingly knocked. On one side is a surface about 3.5 cm in size that is closest to the plane.
Almost closed-round cannonball. A flat surface with a radius of 45 mm. The surface is white.
The years 1935 - 1943 extensive conservation and restoration work was carried out on Kronoberg Castle Ruin (Swedish Heritage Board 93 in Växjö sn) and in connection with it archaeological studies.
Långsmalt bryne med rundade ändar av gulvit och glimmerhaltig skiffer. Rektangulärt tvärsnitt. Avsmalnande i ena änden.
The greater part of a long narrow needle bridge of greyish-white and mica slate. Rectangular cross section. Several deep grinding grooves on the two broad sides.
Close to grey and reddish brown, mica slate. Rectangular cross section thinning towards one end. Flatsides evenly bare.
Irregularly rectangular bryne of white and mica slate. A thin grinding cord on one broad side. Possibly for grinding needles. One end obliquely rejected.
Fragment av ett grått sandstensbryne med kvadratiskt tvärsnitt. Ändparti. På en sida finns två spår efter nålvässning och på en sida två avlånga fördjupningar.
Del av ett grått skifferbryne. En bred och en smal sida planslipade. Vid ena sidan spår efter nålvässning.
Änddel av bryne av grå skiffer. Brott i ena änden och avsmalnande i den andra. Använd på fyra sidor och på de breda sidorna är en smal, djup slipskåra. Möjligen använd för slipning av nålar.
Vitt, men mörkpatinerat glimmerhaltigit skifferbryne. Oregelbundet avlång form med delvis rektanulär genomskärning. Brynet tunnas ut i ena änden och den andra torde ha fungerat som handtag.
Grey white flint carver in the form of production waste. Impurity of quartz on the dorsal side.
The end part of a long narrow, smaller bryne of white-gray and mica slate. Rectangular cutting
Medial part of a narrow bryne in greyish brown sandstone. Rectangular cross section.
The rejection of gray flint with dark patination. The bar bulb on the dorsal side.
Unstructured cut nodule of grey flint with a positional yellowish patination. Natural influence or historical processing.

Part of a round sandstone of light brown sandstone. Slightly more than a quarter preserved. The middle hole has been orthogonal. The sandy surface is still fairly well preserved, the sides rather rough.

Runner of a hand mill made of brown grey sandstone. Has had the shape of a mutilated cone with conical, downward narrowing, middle hole. The bottom smooth but not original. The surface otherwise ground.
Löpare till handkvarn i grå sandsten. Rund med välvd översida och slät undersida. Ett runt mitthål samt runt hål för handtaget. På undersidan är ett rektangulärt urtag tvärs över mitthålet.

Kantstycke av rund behållare i brungrå sandsten. Spår efter invändigt flat botten. Undersidan har rå yta, kanten är avrundad och insidan blankslipad genom nötning. Möjligen del av en stor mortel eller skål med senapskula?
A sandstone fragments of grey sandstone. The grinding surface with has a deep and a few weaker, oblique grinding teeth. For the hissing of spetish objects?
Quantum piece of a round container (?) in brown gray and possibly secondary burnt sandstone. Originally a round recess with 100 to 120 mm diameter.

Ihåligt piphandtag av yngre rödgods med utkragad yttre kant samt del av grund bukdel. Typ B på skaftet, men då det är en stekpanna blir dateringen snarare 1500 - 1550. Rester av gröngul glasyr på kärlets insida.
Fragment av bronsplåt med vikt kant. Spår av bearbetning med mejsel i parrallella rader.

Straight mint fragments of younger red estates with yellow glaze on the edge of the estuary and dark brown glaze on the inside of the shard. Drejränder and black glaze on the outside. Likely part of a bowl due to the decor. Secondary burned…

Mining Fragments of Younger Red Goods with Light Yellow Glacier and White Pipera on the Inside of the Shard. Weak skies on the outside. Likely an edge of a bowl or barrel. Made in southern Scandinavia.
Part of the bottom ring to a bowl of younger red goods. Brown red glaze on the inside of the vessel. Fits with M 17000-2141. Made in southern Scandinavia.

Abdominal fragments of younger red goods with brown yellow glaze on the inside and outside of the vessel. Yellow-white pattern decor of piplera on the outside. Possibly a bowl, carott or similar serving vessel. Made in southern Scandinavia.

Bottom Fragments of Younger Red Goods with Interior Decor of White Piplera. Among other things, concentric circles. Also fragments of green glaze. Likely part of a bowl, barrel or similar serving vessel. Made in southern Scandinavia.

Bottom Fragments of Younger Red Goods. Brown red glaze and decor of white piplera with motif of a rooster within concentric circles on the inside. Smooth outside. Made in southern Scandinavia, but after German role model. About 1550 - 1600.
Secondary burnt coining fragments of younger red estates. Deformed so inside become convex.
Fragment a bowl or a barrel of younger red goods. Part of the bottom, abdomen and estuary. Secondary, hard-burned glaze on the inside of the vessel, but traces of concentric circles of white piplera.

Part of the coining edge of younger red goods with brown glaze on the inside. Decor with white piplera and green glaze, as well as a wide yellow-white stripe on the mouth edge. Outside with tight, profiled lines at the mouth brink.
Abdominal/bottom fragments with a coin-edge of younger red estates. Interior brown glaze and decor with white piplera. Five concentric circles and part of a rooster motif at the bottom.

Part of the coining edge of younger red goods. Interior light brown glaze and decor with white piplera and green glaze. Smooth outside. Made in southern Scandinavia. Gives impression of lying in water.

Abdominal fragments of younger red goods with brown glaze on the inside. Decor with white piplera, concential circles and transverse patterns on the brink. Smooth outside. Made in southern Scandinavia.

Abdominal/bottom fragments of younger red goods with yellow-brown glaze on the inside. Decor with two concentric stripes and transverse patterns with white piplera. Smooth outside. Made in southern Scandinavia.

Part of the coining edge of younger red goods with dark brown and green glaze on the inside. Decorating stripes with white piplera on the brink and on the edge. Doylines on the outside. Made in southern Scandinavia.

Part of a cantilevered coining edge of younger red goods with green-brown glaze on the inside of the vessel. A narrow vulst marks the axis of the vessel and below it is a number of stripes on the otherwise smooth outside.
Abdominal/bottom fragments of younger red estates. Beamed inside with a residue of yellow glaze. Smooth outside with brown glaze. Made in southern Scandinavia.
Part of the coining edge of younger red goods with yellow glaze on the inside of the vessel. Drejkoppled stripes on the outside of the mouth brink. Made in southern Scandinavia.
Abdominal fragments of German younger red goods with reddish-brown glaze and drejänder on the outside of the intersection. Made in western Germany in 1500 - 1599.
Coin fragments of German younger red goods with yellow-brown glaze on the inside of the shard and partly on the outside. Produced western Germany 1500 - 1599. Interview with M 17000-2275 and 2276.

Coin fragments of German younger red goods. White engobe and yellow glaze on the inside as well as the outside of the curve. Possibly part of a bowl or similar household vessel. Made in western Germany in 1550 - 1650.

Abdominal and bottom fragments of younger red goods with dark yellow-green glaze on the inside. Decor stripes with white piplera in the form of a branching plant with round leaves or flowers. Smooth outside with weak lines and flat bottom.

Abdominal/bottom fragments of younger red goods with brown yellow glaze and decor of white piplera on the inside of the vessel. Smooth outside, partly with brown yellow glaze. Made in southern Scandinavia during the 1600s.
Abdominal/bottom fragments of German younger white goods. Drejrutlat with white engobe and yellow glaze on the inside and brown engobe with decor of spotted yellow glaze on the outside of the shard.

Coin plate for a knife slide. Made of a smooth blank with engraved ornation in the form of parallel lines, arranged in groups of two (top and bottom) and three in the middle. The leaves have been laid about castles and hopled.
Coin fragments of German, brightly younger red goods. White engobe and remnants of yellow glaze on the inside of the notch, and remnants of bright greenish-yellow engobe on the outside.

Part of a hollow spun horn (wind instrument). Cylindrical tube with slightly curved shape. Younger Red Goods. Made in the German city of Lübeck or southern parts of Schleswieg-Holstein in the 15th-16th century.
